title: Effects of training and anthropometric factors on marathon and 100 km ultramarathon race performance
journal: Open Access Journal of Sports Medicine
population: Marathoners and 100 km ultramarathoners (large cohort; bivariate and multiple regression of training and anthropometric variables vs race pace)
findings: A combination of training volume and intensity was suitable for predicting both marathon and 100 km race pace.
Training volume was more important than training pace for predicting 100 km performance, whereas the opposite held for the marathon.
Mean weekly training distance and mean training pace were the key predictor variables for both marathon and 100 km performance.
Higher body-fat percentage negatively affected 42 km and 100 km performance; below about 15% body fat, performance could be predicted solely from training indices.
A combination of training volume and intensity predicted marathon and 100 km race pace.
Higher body fat percentage hurt both 42 km and 100 km performance; below 15% body fat, performance could be predicted solely from training indices.
Mean weekly training distance and mean training pace were the key predictors for both distances.
limitations: Observational and correlational, self-reported training; sample size not stated in the abstract; body-fat finding applies to a mostly male recreational cohort; association is not proof that raising volume improves performance.
implications: For 100 km goals, weight weekly volume above training pace in progression priorities (volume first, then pace); for marathon, the reverse.

Use mean weekly training distance and mean training pace as the two inputs of a simple race-pace sanity predictor for 100 km, fitted locally on the athlete's own data; coefficients are not in the abstract.
The plan generator should set no body-composition target.
Use both weekly distance and training pace as inputs for marathon and 100 km predictions; do not hard-code which dominates for ultras given the conflicting 2010 paper.
Show uncertainty wider for ultra predictions.

verification.notes: Crossref (2015-04) title and journal match; Crossref lists Knechtle first but PubMed/Europe PMC list Tanda G, Knechtle B and the researcher's order was kept. Abstract re-read from Europe PMC; sample size not stated so null.
